title: The bird that made Darwin sick

scenes.headline: The bird that made Darwin feel sick
“The sight of a feather in a peacock’s tail, whenever I gaze at it, makes me sick!”
scenes.body: Charles Darwin to Asa Gray, 3 April 1860

caption:
One feather nearly broke a theory.

Darwin's fix was a second force alongside natural selection: traits can spread simply because mates prefer them. He set it out in full in The Descent of Man (1871).

Source: Darwin Correspondence Project (letter 2743); Britannica.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Historic-discovery storytime carried by subtitle chunks over one continuous peacock-display clip, with the real letter quote as a quote card; told through a bird every Indian viewer knows.
